statement: Every commit the server confirmed with 200 + sequence is present after SIGKILL crash and restart; recovered rows equal the independent client-side model exactly.
method: independent row model vs /query after restart; journal decode contiguity base+1..head

statement: A commit whose response was not consumed before the crash has no client-decidable outcome; ground truth is established only by recovery inspection. Both resolutions were run: a large commit killed before the journal write was LOST; small commits killed after the write/fsync were DURABLE despite the missing confirmation.
method: raw-socket commit + SIGKILL at controlled delays and write-set sizes; post-restart /query + independent journal decode; all-or-nothing spot-check of the write set

statement: Recovered state = checkpoint image [1..7] + journal suffix [8..8] = exactly the confirmed commit prefix [1..8]; no gap, no extra.
method: independent image decode (digest, sequence) + independent journal frame table (contiguity) + row model at head and at checkpoint sequence

statement: Restored state = backup image [1..8] + restored-instance journal [9..9]; the source's post-backup commit (seq 9, row 11) is NOT part of the restored prefix.
method: independent backup decode + restored journal header/base decode + row model comparison; post-backup row absence check
notes: backup.sequence=8, restored journal base=8, restored head=9

statement: A 3-byte incomplete tail is truncated at startup; the committed prefix is unchanged (recovered_tail_bytes=3, head and rows identical to pre-append).
method: append 3 bytes to a journal copy; restart; stats + row model + journal re-decode

statement: A single-bit flip inside a complete frame (last frame or middle frame) makes startup FAIL with a checksum error; the journal is not silently truncated or modified.
method: byte flip on copies; run binary; check exit code, stderr, and file hash before/after

statement: After restore, change cursors below history_base=8 are rejected (410), even though current row values can be identical to a consumer's last-seen values (row2 amplitude unchanged while transitions at seq 4,5 are unreachable). Cursors at the base are accepted but continue on a DIFFERENT lineage: sequence 9 exists on both sides with different transaction ids/content.
method: raw /changes calls on source and restored instances; transaction-id comparison at the same sequence number
notes: 410 for cursor<base; 200 for cursor==base with new-lineage records
